3. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the complainant petitioner submits that the Magistrate and the Additional District Magistrate while pronouncing the judgment categorically stated the involvement of the accused opposite parties that they inflicted bleeding injury and took away the valuable but the Revisional court without considering all these aspects acquitted all the accused persons which requires to be interfered by this court. He further submits that the impugned judgment passed by the Sessions Judge is based on presumption and it is beyond the scope of Section 335 and 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. 

 6. We have gone through the impugned judgment and the lower court records. It appears from the judgment passed by the Magistrate, 2nd Class that the Magistrate specifically stated the involvement of the opposite parties and he has also referred the deposition made by the dr. P.W.5 the injuries inflicted upon the victim and the other witnesses as such it has been corroborated the depositions made by the complainant and there is no contradiction in their deposition. There is nothing to be interfered passed by the Magistrate 2nd Class, however, the accused preferred appeal and on appeal the Additional District Magistrate by exercising his judicial mind dismissed the appeal. Thereafter the accused preferred revisional application before the Sessions Judge. The Sessions Judge on a mere surmises and conjectures set aside the order passed by the court below and acquitted all the accused persons. The Sessions Judge while disposing of the revisional application though found that Additional District Magistrate applied his judicial mind but disbelieved the witnesses which is not at all maintainable. The lower appellate Court also appeared to have not discussed the evidences as adduced by the witnesses.
